content: 1. Stiripentol can act as both an inhibitor and an inducer. When co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates, monitor for either increased or decreased effects. Adjust therapy as needed. 2. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Consider reducing the dose of P-glycoprotein substrates if adverse reactions occur. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of streptomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Co-administration of sufentanil SL with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including life-threatening respiratory depression. 7. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus ointment by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting both hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Talazoparib is a P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrate, and co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to talazoparib. 13. Ritonavir and tamoxifen interact by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. This decreases the conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolites, such as endoxifen, which have significantly higher estrogen receptor affinity. Reduced endoxifen levels may lead to poor clinical outcomes. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Lopinavir increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ritonavir increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of teniposide by inhibiting both the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Ritonavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Ritonavir increases tenofovir DF levels by decreasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Terbinafine increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ritonavir increases the effects of tetrabenazine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Reduce the tetrabenazine dose by 50% when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 28. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 29. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 30. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Lopinavir increases the levels of ticagrelor by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ticagrelor is metabolized by CYP3A4/5, and its use should be avoided with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 32. Ritonavir increases the levels of tiagabine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Ritonavir increases the levels of timolol by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity, including hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. 34. Lopinavir increases the levels of timolol by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity, including PR prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 35. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Lopinavir increases the levels of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to unconjugated MMAE, raising the risk of adverse effects. 37. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both ritonavir and tipranavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 38. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Tolvaptan also increases ritonavir levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Ritonavir increases the levels of toremifene by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Toremifene metabolism may be inhibited by drugs that inhibit CYP3A4 hepatic enzymes. 43. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tramadol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. A reduced tramadol dose or adjustment of dosing interval may be required due to the increased risk of serious adverse events, including seizures and serotonin syndrome. 44. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Trazodone decreases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Triclabendazole and lopinavir both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases trimipramine levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Tucatinib increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 50. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 51. Ublituximab decreases ritonavir effects due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 52. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Dose adjustment is recommended when ubrogepant is co-administered with moderate or weak CYP3A4 inducers. 53. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases upadacitinib levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 55. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Valbenazine and lopinavir both increase the QTc interval. Reduce the valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 56. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of valsartan by decreasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Valsartan is a substrate of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1 and the efflux transporter MRP2. Co-administration with inhibitors of these transporters may increase systemic exposure to valsartan. 57. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. The vardenafil dose may need to be reduced when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 58. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day if weight >50 kg. 59. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Vemurafenib also increases ritonavir levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Lopinavir increases the levels of venlafaxine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases venlafaxine levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 61. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Verapamil also increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Verapamil increases lopinavir levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Both fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are CYP3A4 substrates, and co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure.
